Grammy-winning singer Burna Boy has extended his record as Nigeria’s most-nominated artiste at the Grammy Awards, with 14 career nominations, following the announcement of the 2027 nominees. The 2027 Grammy nominations, announced on Monday, November 16, added to the career totals of several Nigerian music stars, with Tems emerging as the country’s most nominated artiste in the latest edition after receiving four nods. Here is a look at the Nigerian artistes who have accumulated the most Grammy nominations over the years, based on their career totals: 1. Burna Boy — 14 nominations Burna Boy earned his latest nomination for “Dìá Dìá”, his collaboration with Colombian singer Shakira, in the Best Global Music Performance category at the 2027 Grammys. The recognition takes his career tally to 14, including his 2021 win for Best Global Music Album with Twice as Tall. His first nomination came in 2020, when African Giant was nominated for Best World Music Album. He received another nomination in 2021 for Twice as Tall, which won the Best Global Music Album award. His subsequent nominations include “Do Yourself”, his collaboration with Angélique Kidjo, for Best Global Music Performance, and Justin Bieber’s Justice for Album of the Year in 2022 (on which he featured on the track ‘Loved by You’). In 2023, “Last Last” was nominated for Best Global Music Performance, while Love, Damini received a nomination for Best Global Music Album. Burna Boy earned four nominations in 2024: “Sittin’ On Top Of The World” featuring 21 Savage for Best Melodic Rap Performance; “Alone” for Best Global Music Performance; “City Boys” for Best African Music Performance; and I Told Them… for Best Global Music Album. He received another nomination in 2025 for “Higher” in the Best African Music Performance category. In 2026, “Love” was nominated for Best African Music Performance, while No Sign of Weakness earned a nod for Best Global Music Album. 2. Tems — 12 nominations Tems received four nominations at the 2027 Grammys, taking her career total to 12. Her song “Big Daddy” was nominated for Best African Music Performance, while her album Love Is a Kingdom earned a nod for Best Global Music Album. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Her first Grammy nomination came in 2022 for her contribution to Wizkid’s “Essence”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance. In 2023, she earned three nominations through her contribution to Future’s “Wait For U”, featuring Drake. The song was nominated for Best Melodic Rap Performance, which it won, and Best Rap Song. She also shared an Album of the Year nomination for Beyoncé’s Renaissance. In 2024, Tems received a nomination for Best Song Written for Visual Media for “Lift Me Up”, from the Black Panther: Wakanda Forever soundtrack. She earned three nominations in 2025: Best R&B Song for “Burning”, Best African Music Performance for “Love Me JeJe”, which won the category, and Best Global Music Album for Born in the Wild. 3. Wizkid — 7 nominations Wizkid has received seven Grammy nominations and won once. His latest recognition came through “Jogodo”, his collaboration with Asake, which was nominated for Best African Music Performance at the 2027 awards. His first nomination came in 2017 through Drake’s album Views, which was nominated for Album of the Year. In 2021, he won Best Music Video for “Brown Skin Girl”, his collaboration with Beyoncé, Blue Ivy Carter and Saint Jhn. He received two nominations in 2022: Best Global Music Album for Made in Lagos: Deluxe Edition and Best Global Music Performance for “Essence”, his collaboration with Tems. In 2026, he earned another nomination in the same category for “Gimme Dat”, his collaboration with Ayra Starr. 4. Davido — 6 nominations Davido’s six Grammy nominations have come across four consecutive editions of the awards. He received three nominations in 2024 for “Feel” in the Best Global Music Performance category, “Unavailable” featuring Musa Keys in the Best African Music Performance category, and his album Timeless for Best Global Music Album. In 2025, he was nominated for Best African Music Performance for “Sensational”, his collaboration with American singer Chris Brown and Nigerian singer Lojay. He earned another nomination in 2026 for “With You”, his collaboration with Omah Lay, in the Best African Music Performance category. His latest nomination is for his album Oriadé, which will compete for Best Global Music Album at the 2027 Grammys. 4. Femi Kuti — 6 nominations Afrobeat musician Femi Kuti is also on six Grammy nominations. His first came in 2003, when his album Fight to Win was nominated for Best World Music Album. He received another nomination in 2010 for Day by Day in the Best Contemporary World Music Album category. This was followed by nominations for Africa for Africa in 2012 and No Place for My Dream in 2014, both in the Best World Music Album category. In 2022, Femi received two nominations: Best Global Music Performance for “Pà Pá Pà” and Best Global Music Album for Legacy +, his joint project with his son, Made Kuti. 6. Asake — 4 nominations Asake has received four Grammy nominations, all in the Best African Music Performance category. His first came in 2024 for “Amapiano”, his collaboration with Olamide. He received another nomination in 2025 for “MMS”, his collaboration with Wizkid. At the 2027 Grammys, Asake earned two nominations in the same category: one for his song “Gratitude” and another for “Jogodo”, his collaboration with Wizkid. 6. Ayra Starr — 4 nominations Ayra Starr also has four Grammy nominations. Her first came in 2024 for her song “Rush”, which was nominated for Best African Music Performance. In 2026, she received another nomination in the category for “Gimme Dat”, her collaboration with Wizkid. For the 2027 edition, she earned two nominations: Best African Music Performance for “Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?)”, her collaboration with Beninese singer Angélique Kidjo, and Best Global Music Album for Starrgirl. The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on February 7, 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, United States.
